WHY ZUEGER

You don't rack up 77 blocked shots in a single season by accident. You do it by putting your body in front of danger so your teammates don't have to. That's not a hockey stat — that's a leadership philosophy.

📚
Scholar First

AHCA All-American Scholar. AHA All-Academic Team. January Scholar-Athlete of the Month. His TAC officer called him "professional, generous, and always willing to help others." He doesn't just meet the standard. He raises it.

🌍
Global Experience

Most cadets spend their summer on post. Easton spent his in Vicenza, Italy as a Platoon Sergeant with the 173rd Airborne. Then pivoted to a management consulting internship at Kearney. Equally lethal in both arenas.

⚡
Earned, Not Granted

Elk Point, South Dakota doesn't produce many D1 athlete-scholars. From the Sioux City Musketeers to Army Black Knights, everything Easton has he built himself. He knows what it means to work for something from nothing.

🥀
Relentlessly Multidimensional

Scuba certified. Hockey defenseman. Management consultant. Airborne platoon leader. Researcher. The First Captain must represent every kind of soldier. Easton Zueger might literally be every kind of soldier simultaneously.

🎯

His TAC officer said it plainly: "others look to him as a role model." You don't get to be a role model — it's earned by how you carry yourself when nobody's watching. Easton has been carrying himself that way since Day 1.

// COMMITMENTS

THE PLATFORM

01
Cadet Welfare, No Asterisks

The Corps runs on people. A First Captain who has been in the trenches — on the ice, in the weight room, at 0530 formation — understands what the Corps actually needs. Easton will fight for quality-of-life improvements that have real impact.

02
Hold the Standard, Earn the Respect

Standards at West Point exist for a reason. Easton believes in enforcing the standard not through fear but through example. When your First Captain has blocked 77 shots in a season and aced every class, the standard feels like a baseline.

03
Bridge Between Corps and Staff

The First Captain's most important job is translation — making sure the concerns of 4,400 cadets reach the people who can act on them. Easton's consulting experience taught him how to synthesize complex problems into clear recommendations.

04
Compete Everywhere, Represent Always

The First Captain is the face of 4,400 cadets to the Army, the nation, and the world. Easton has already represented West Point in Italy, in consulting boardrooms, on research stages, and in Division I arenas. He knows how to show up.
